title: Circadian rhythms remain temperature compensated during a Q neuron–induced hibernation-like state in mice
experiments_summary: The study employed multiple complementary in vivo and in vitro approaches to examine circadian clock behavior during QIH (Q neuron-induced hibernation-like state). (1) Behavioral rhythm monitoring: Qrfp-iCre mice received stereotaxic bilateral injections of AAV10-Ef1a-DIO-hM3D(Gq)-mCherry or control AAV into the AVPe. QIH was induced via intraperitoneal CNO (1 mg/kg) under constant darkness (DD). Locomotor activity was recorded with infrared sensors and wheel-running activity with running wheels, both in 1-min bins. Activity onset phases were computed pre- and post-QIH using ClockLab, and phase shifts, period changes, and individual variability were assessed using Welch's t-test, F-test, and Pearson's correlation. (2) Core body temperature rhythms: Thermal loggers (iButton or NanoTag) were implanted intraperitoneally in mice. Temperature rhythms were compared between pre-QIH and post-QIH periods under DD, with amplitude and period calculated by sine-curve fitting and phase shifts analyzed by two-way ANOVA. (3) Brain temperature measurement: An ultra-thin thermocouple probe was implanted near the SCN via a guide cannula, enabling simultaneous brain and core body temperature recording at 2 Hz in freely moving mice during QIH, allowing verification that SCN temperature dropped to ~25°C. (4) In vivo electrophysiology: A microdrive with 8 independently adjustable tetrodes was implanted targeting the SCN in Qrfp-iCre mice also receiving AVPe viral injections. Single-unit firing rates were recorded continuously across LD, DD, QIH, and post-QIH conditions (10 min/hour over 48-h blocks). Only units exhibiting circadian fluctuations in both LD and DD were analyzed. Spike sorting was performed using SpikeSort3D, and firing rate data were fit to sine curves to extract amplitude and period. Tetrode locations were histologically confirmed post-experiment. (5) In vivo PER2::LUC bioluminescence recording: Qrfp-iCre/PER2::LUC mice with AVPe AAV injections received intraperitoneally implanted osmotic pumps continuously infusing D-luciferin. Whole-body bioluminescence was imaged every 10 min with a CCD camera (MIIS system) under DD. CNO was injected on day 2 of recording; bioluminescence signals were detrended and fit to sine curves to determine phase, amplitude, and period pre-, during, and post-QIH. (6) In vitro SCN and kidney slice cultures: SCN and kidney slices (~150 µm) were prepared from PER2::LUC homozygous mice and cultured on Millicell inserts with luciferin-containing medium. Cultures were maintained at 37°C or 25°C, or subjected to temperature-shift protocols (37→25°C and 25→37°C). Bioluminescence was recorded every 10 min with a luminometer (Kronos Dio). Data were detrended and fit to sine curves to calculate amplitude and period, and phase-resetting effects of temperature changes were assessed. (7) Immunohistochemistry: After behavioral or electrophysiological experiments, mice were perfused with 4% PFA; brain sections were stained with anti-mCherry and anti-c-Fos antibodies to verify viral expression in AVPe and SCN targeting.
